newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Home mortgage loans continue to grow in Jan - HKMA.
newsitem.headline: Home mortgage loans continue to grow in Jan - HKMA.

text.p: The volume of residential mortgage loans in Hong Kong continued to grow in January, Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) data showed on Wednesday.
In a statement, the HKMA said total outstanding mortgage lending by the 33 institutions surveyed rose by 2.6 percent to HK$338.9 billion.
The growth rate was higher than the monthly average of 1.7 percent over the last 12 months, it said.

"The rapid growth in lending reflected the increased activity in both the primary and secondary residential property markets in December and January," David Carse, deputy chief executive of the HKMA, was quoted as saying.
"In particular the primary market accounted for an increased share of the new lending in January as a large number of new properties were put on to the market."
The 12-month average of outstanding loans showed an annualised growth rate of 20.6 percent, compared with 18.9 percent in December, the HKMA said.
The amount of new loans approved but not yet drawn increased by 18.3 percent to $15 billion in January, reflecting the volume of market activity in that month, it said.
"In view of lending already in the pipeline, we expect the growth of residential mortgage loans will continue at a rapid rate in February," Carse said.
Lending for the purchase of properties in China increased by 3.1 percent to HK$6.5 billion in January.
Gross loans made in January decreased both in number from 310 to 207 and in amount from HK$410 million to HK$132 million.
New loans approved in January increased in number to 263 from 212 and in amount to HK$224 million from HK$157 million.
